가방.x: There are books and a wallet in my bag.
가방.e: From Japanese kaban (bag). Covers any bag: backpack, purse, briefcase.

한국어.x: Korean is fun but a little difficult.
한국어.e: 한국 (Korea) + 어 (language). Add -어 to a country for its language: 중국어, 일본어.
한국어.t: Pronounced [한구거]. 한국말 is the more conversational word for the same thing.

듣다.forms: 들어요 · 들었어요 · 들을 거예요 · 들으세요 (ㄷ irregular)
듣다.m: to listen, to hear; to take (a class)
듣다.x: I listen to Korean music every day.
듣다.e: 수업을 듣다 = to take a class.
듣다.t: ㄷ irregular: ㄷ turns into ㄹ before a vowel — 듣다 → 들어요.

일찍.forms: 일찍 + verb: 일찍 일어나요, 일찍 자요
일찍.x: I have to get up early tomorrow.
일찍.e: Opposite of 늦게 (late). 일찍 일어나요 = I get up early.
일찍.t: 일찍 = early (time); 빨리 = quickly (speed). Don't mix them up.

태국.ex: 태국 음식은 맵고 달고 정말 맛있어요.
태국.x: Thai food is spicy, sweet, and really delicious.
태국.e: Literally 'great country'; -국 = country: 한국, 중국, 미국.

곳.e: Also works as a counter: 한 곳, 두 곳.

싣다.forms: 실어요 · 실었어요 · 실을 거예요 · 실으세요 (ㄷ irregular)
싣다.m: to load, to put (in a vehicle); to publish (an article)
싣다.ex: 이사하는 날 짐을 트럭에 모두 실었어요.
싣다.x: On moving day we loaded all our things onto the truck.
싣다.e: Also used for newspapers: 신문에 글을 싣다 = to run an article.

소식.x: Yesterday I heard the news that my friend is getting married.
소식.e: Literally 'waning and growing' — word of how things are going.
소식.t: 소식 is personal news or word from someone; 뉴스 is news from the media.

회식.x: We have a team dinner this evening.
회식.t: 회식 is a big part of Korean office culture and often involves drinking.

도장.x: Please stamp your seal on this document.
도장.e: A carved name seal, traditionally used in Korea instead of a signature.
도장.t: Homonym: 도장 also means a martial-arts gym, as in 태권도 도장.

건강 검진.ex: 우리 회사는 매년 건강 검진을 받아요.
건강 검진.x: Everyone at our company gets a health checkup every year.

환갑.ex: 올해 아버지 환갑이라서 가족 여행을 가요.
환갑.x: It's my father's 60th birthday this year, so we're going on a family trip.
환갑.e: Literally 'returning to 갑': the 60-year cycle of the traditional calendar starts over.

자극.ex: 친구의 성공이 저에게 좋은 자극이 됐어요.
자극.x: My friend's success was a good motivation for me.
자극.e: Literally 'pierce with a spear' — something that pokes you into action.
자극.t: 자극적인 음식 means very spicy or salty food.

면접관.x: The interviewer asked me about my experience.

실업.x: Youth unemployment is a serious problem these days.
실업.t: 실업 is used for society-level statistics; for one person losing a job, 실직 is more common.

민속.ex: 민속 마을에서 옛날 한국 집을 구경했어요.
민속.x: I looked around old Korean houses at a folk village.
민속.t: Mostly used before nouns: 민속놀이 'folk games', 민속 박물관 'folk museum'.

소득.x: My income went up a little this year compared to last year.

어린이집.x: Every morning I drop my child off at daycare and go to work.
어린이집.t: Pronounced [어리니집]: the ㄴ links into the next syllable. Daycare takes children from infancy up to age five, while 유치원 is for ages three to five.

공식적.x: The government officially announced the news.
공식적.e: 공식 'official' + -적 '-al'; -적 turns nouns into describing words: 사회적, 경제적.
공식적.t: Use 공식적인 before a noun and 공식적으로 as an adverb meaning 'officially'.

건축.x: He majored in architecture in college.
건축.t: 건축하다 means to build a building; 건설 is used for large projects like roads, bridges and dams.

열정.ex: 그 선생님은 가르치는 일에 열정이 많아요.
열정.x: That teacher is very passionate about teaching.

본성.x: When people get angry, their true nature shows.

벗기다.m: to take off (someone's clothes, shoes); to peel, strip
벗기다.x: I peeled the apple thinly with a knife.
벗기다.e: Causative of 벗다 'to take off': making something come off.

쫓겨나다.m: to be kicked out, be thrown out, be expelled
쫓겨나다.x: I couldn't pay rent, so I got kicked out of my place.

독창성.ex: 이 작품은 독창성이 뛰어나다는 평가를 받았어요.
독창성.x: This work was praised for its outstanding originality.
독창성.e: Literally 'the quality of creating alone'. -성 = '-ness/-ity': 가능성, 중요성.

일정표.x: Before the trip, I made a detailed itinerary.
일정표.t: Pronounced [일쩡표] — ㅈ tenses after ㄹ in Sino-Korean words.

과속.x: I paid a fine for speeding yesterday.

보정.ex: 사진을 너무 많이 보정해서 제 얼굴 같지 않아요.
보정.x: I edited the photo so much that it doesn't look like my face.
보정.t: 보정 앱 is a photo-editing app. Outside photos, 보정 속옷 means shapewear.

심경.ex: 그는 기자들 앞에서 자신의 심경을 밝혔습니다.
심경.x: He shared his feelings in front of reporters.
심경.t: Formal and news-like: 심경을 밝히다 'express one's feelings', 심경의 변화 'change of heart'.

번영.ex: 모든 국민이 나라의 평화와 번영을 바랍니다.
번영.x: All citizens wish for the nation's peace and prosperity.

열강.ex: 19세기 말 조선은 서구 열강의 압력을 받았습니다.
열강.x: In the late 19th century, Joseon came under pressure from the Western powers.
열강.e: Literally 'the row of strong ones' — powerful states lined up together.
열강.t: Mostly a history word for 19th–20th century imperial powers; for today use 강대국.

이룩하다.ex: 한국은 짧은 기간에 놀라운 경제 성장을 이룩했습니다.
이룩하다.x: Korea achieved remarkable economic growth in a short period.
이룩하다.e: Related to 이루다 'to achieve' but weightier, used for big historic accomplishments.
이룩하다.t: Pronounced [이루카다] — ㄱ and ㅎ merge into ㅋ.

조장하다.m: to encourage (something bad), to foster, to fuel
조장하다.ex: 일부 광고는 과소비를 조장한다는 비판을 받습니다.
조장하다.x: Some ads are criticized for encouraging overspending.
조장하다.e: From a Chinese fable: a farmer pulled sprouts up to 'help them grow' and killed them.
조장하다.t: Almost always negative: 갈등을 조장하다, 불안을 조장하다 — use 장려하다 for good things.

듬직하다.ex: 우리 큰아들은 정말 듬직해서 마음이 놓여요.
듬직하다.x: My oldest son is really dependable, so I feel at ease.
듬직하다.e: Pairs with 믿음직하다 'trustworthy' — both describe someone you can lean on.
듬직하다.t: Pronounced [듬지카다]; often used for someone physically solid and steady, like 듬직한 체격 'a sturdy build'.

굴욕.ex: 우리 팀은 꼴찌 팀에게 지는 굴욕을 맛봤어요.
굴욕.x: Our team suffered the humiliation of losing to the last-place team.
굴욕.e: Literally 'bending in disgrace' — being forced to bow.
굴욕.t: Pronounced [구룍]; casually, 굴욕 사진 is an embarrassingly unflattering photo.

회생.ex: 그 회사는 법원에 기업 회생 절차를 신청했습니다.
회생.x: The company filed for corporate rehabilitation with the court.
회생.e: Literally 'returning to life' — also used for patients and economies.

변동비.ex: 생산량이 늘면 재료비 같은 변동비도 늘어납니다.
변동비.x: When output rises, variable costs like materials rise too.

필력.m: writing skill, the power of one's pen
필력.ex: 그 작가는 데뷔작부터 탄탄한 필력을 보여 주었어요.
필력.x: That author showed solid writing skill from the very first book.
필력.e: Literally 'brush power' — how forcefully and skillfully someone writes.
필력.t: ㄹ + ㄹ is pronounced as a clear double L: [필력], pillyeok.

자명하다.ex: 노력 없이 성공할 수 없다는 것은 자명한 사실이에요.
자명하다.x: It's a self-evident fact that you can't succeed without effort.
자명하다.t: Typically 자명한 사실 or 자명한 이치 'a self-evident truth'.

짓누르다.forms: 짓눌러요 · 짓눌렀어요 · 짓누를 거예요 · 짓누르세요 (르 irregular)
짓누르다.m: to press down hard, to crush; to weigh on, to oppress
짓누르다.x: The pressure of the exam weighed heavily on me.
짓누르다.t: Pronounced [진누르다] — nasalization; the passive 짓눌리다 'to be crushed' is very common.
